banner.none: No language model provider is connected.
banner.connectedNote: This model rephrases the assistant's answers. It never queries the database itself: the search is performed upstream, with the permissions of the person asking, and the cited sources always come from that search — never from text produced by the model. If the call fails, the assistant falls back to the search-only answer.
banner.noneNote: The five agents still answer, by searching the platform's own data with the permissions of the person asking. Setting HF_API_KEY in the server's environment adds rephrasing; it does not switch on the feature, which already works.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: An agent reads with the permissions of whoever queries it: it can never surface a row the person could not open themselves. Enabling an agent records the intent; agents marked "operational" already answer, by searching the platform's own data, with no language model at all.
agents.promptPlaceholder: Instruction given to the agent. The rule that already applies without a provider: every answer cites its source, or admits it found nothing.

ai.footnote: The settings on this form are saved but do not yet drive the assistant: it reads its configuration from the server's environment (HF_API_KEY, HF_MODEL, HF_BASE_URL), not from this table. ai.footnoteTailConnected: , then have that answer rephrased by the connected model.

whatSwitchDoes.title: What the switch does
whatSwitchDoes.body: It durably records the intended mode for each integration, with an entry in the audit log. That is the intent declared by the administration.

whatSwitchDoesNot.title: What it does not do
whatSwitchDoesNot.body: It does not connect any system: the real address comes from the server's environment, fixed at deployment. No Entra ID tenant, no HR system and no SMTP relay answers on this deployment — the "Test" button says so explicitly rather than showing a reassuring green tick.

organization.footnote: This screen defines the skeleton: units, positions and reporting lines. It does not place anyone — assigning an employee to a position is HR's responsibility, and duplicating it here would give the same action two implementations. Archiving a unit is refused while it still holds active units or positions: the error message states what remains to be moved.

roles.title: Roles and permissions
roles.subtitle: The role × module × action matrix: what each profile may read, write, validate and delete.
roles.builtinNote: These four profiles are defined in the platform's code, not in the database: every request checks the caller's rights, and querying a table at that point would put a database round trip at the heart of every access check. They are therefore viewable here but only editable through deployment. For a different need, create a custom role.

form.codeHintExisting: An existing role's code cannot be changed.
form.name: Name

roles.customEmptyDetail: The four built-in profiles cover everyday use. Create a custom role for a need none of them describes — an external auditor, for instance, who would read without ever writing.
roles.customFootnote: A custom role is saved durably, with its permissions validated against the platform's catalogue. It is not yet assignable to an account: assignment goes through the four built-in codes, the only ones the authorisation layer recognises. Defining the role is the durable part; wiring it to assignment is a change to that layer, not to this screen.

inEffect.title: In effect
inEffect.subtitle: Values read from the configuration validated at start-up. They change at deployment, not from this screen.
inEffect.passwordsDetail: Minimum length: {{length}} characters. Hashed with Argon2id, never stored or logged in any other form.
inEffect.sessionsDetail: {{hours}}-hour duration, extended at most once per {{minutes}}-minute window. Immediate revocation on the next request.
inEffect.encryptionDetail: Exchanges encrypted in transit (TLS). Encryption at rest depends on the host and cannot be verified from the application.
inEffect.replayProtectionDetail: Every mutation requires a CSRF token, and login attempts are rate-limited. Access denials are logged.

provisioning.footnote: This page observes the handoff, it does not carry it out: creating an account is done on <0>Accounts</0>, and assigning it to a position is HR's responsibility. No automatic reminder is sent — no scheduler runs in the application, and no SMTP relay is connected. The waiting times above are therefore to be read, not waited on.

entraSync.detail: No Entra ID directory is connected to this deployment: there is no tenant to import accounts from. A "Synchronise" button could here only do nothing, or invent people.
